n: A second, undated oracle against Egypt.

f.w: The word of the LORD came again unto me
f.g: Verses 1–19 are the only undated oracle against Egypt.

n: “Wail! Alas for the day!”

f.g: “Alas for the day!”—“worth” is old English for “be.”

n: The day of the Lord is near—a day of clouds and doom for the nations. The phrase, often used against Israel, now applies to Egypt.

f.w: the day of the LORD is near

n: A sword will strike Egypt, and Cush (Nubia) will writhe in anguish as Egypt’s people are carried off and its foundations torn down.
Egypt’s allies—Cush, Put, Lud, Arabia, Libya, and others in league—will fall with her.

f.w: the men of the land that is in league
f.g: Possibly “the people of the covenant land”—even Jews living in Egypt.

n: Those who support Egypt will fall; her proud power will collapse from Migdol to Syene.
Egypt will lie desolate among other ruined lands.

f.w: desolate in the midst of the countries that are desolate

n: When God sets Egypt on fire and her helpers are crushed, they will know he is the Lord.

f.w: I have set a fire in Egypt

n: Messengers will go out by ship (up the Nile) to terrify complacent Cush.

f.w: messengers go forth from me in ships

n: God will end Egypt’s hordes through Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.
He and his ruthless army will come to destroy the land and fill it with the slain.
God will dry up the Nile’s channels and sell the land to evil men. Without the Nile, Egypt cannot live.

f.w: I will make the rivers dry

n: Idols will be destroyed in Memphis, and there will be no more native prince over Egypt. Indeed, after the Persian conquest, foreign rulers governed Egypt for most of its history for many centuries.

f.g: Memphis, ancient capital of Egypt near modern Cairo.

f.w: there shall be no more a prince of the land of Egypt

n: Judgment will fall city by city: Pathros (Upper Egypt), Zoan (Tanis), and No (Thebes).

f.g: Thebes (modern Luxor), Upper Egypt’s great capital.

n: God’s fury will fall on Sin (Pelusium), Egypt’s border fortress, and on the crowds of Thebes.

f.g: Pelusium, a fortress guarding Egypt’s northeast frontier.

n: Fire in Egypt: Pelusium will writhe, Thebes will be breached, and Memphis will face constant distress.
The young men of On (Heliopolis) and Pi-beseth (Bubastis) will die, and the cities’ people go captive.

f.g: On or Heliopolis, center of sun worship; “Aven” means “wickedness,” a pun.
Bubastis, a Delta city devoted to a cat goddess.

n: At Tahpanhes, where Jewish refugees (including Jeremiah) had fled, the day will turn dark when Egypt’s power is broken.

f.g: Tahpanhes, a frontier city in the eastern Delta.

n: Thus God will judge Egypt, and they will know he is the Lord.
A new dated oracle: April 587 BC, about three months after 29:1, shortly after Babylon drove back Pharaoh’s relief army.

f.w: in the eleventh year, in the first month, in the seventh day

n: God has broken Pharaoh’s arm, and it won’t be bandaged or splinted to hold a sword again. Pharaoh Hophra’s attempt to relieve Jerusalem had failed.

f.w: I have broken the arm of Pharaoh

n: God will break both his arms—the strong one and the injured one—so the sword falls from his hand.

f.w: the strong, and that which was broken

n: The Egyptians will be scattered among the nations.
God will strengthen Babylon’s arms and put his own sword in its hand, while Pharaoh groans like a mortally wounded man.

f.w: put my sword in his hand

n: Babylon’s arms will be strong and Pharaoh’s will drop. Then all will know that the Lord, not Babylon’s gods, directed history.

f.w: he shall stretch it out upon the land of Egypt

n: The oracle closes as it began, with scattering and the recognition of the Lord.

f.w: they shall know that I am the LORD
